sections.overview: A marine snailfish in Liparidae, it is known from off northern Chile in the southeastern Pacific.
sections.identification: The original description notes unusually large, narrow teeth that curve inward; its name refers to this distinctive dentition.
sections.habitat: The known specimen came from about 800 m depth above a much deeper seafloor; this single record does not define the species’ full depth range.
sections.diet: The consulted sources do not report what it eats.
sections.behavior: No species-specific behavioral observations are reported in the consulted accounts.
sections.reproduction: The consulted sources provide no reproductive observations.
sections.ecology: The species is known from a single type specimen, leaving its ecology largely undocumented. Its eastern-Pacific congener P. cathetostomus is named for its nearly vertical mouth and jaw, rather than the unusual teeth emphasized here.
sections.conservation: The consulted FishBase page lists it as not evaluated by the IUCN.
